reason: Class of work: diagnosing a Metaform web page that freezes or a web server whose memory or CPU keeps growing. The episode started from guessed endpoints (404s) without using the server's slow-request log, and no existing skill covers web GUI hangs (the page-hot-path and event-handler skills cover per-frame JS and idle CPU only).

This episode showed the restart readiness failure was caused by a page request burst starving the server, and that the fix belongs in the burst (batched lookups, no volatile-field churn), not the probe timeout. The hang-diagnosis skill is the one loaded for this class of work and lacked these pitfalls.

The starvation fix changed startup order in web/server.py: listening now comes before background services. Future startup-race diagnoses must know the order, or they will re-add blocking work ahead of the listen.
The review episode measured store latency on a copy of the live home; that method is the reusable part and belongs with the hang-diagnosis rules.
Its frozen-page and growing-server diagnosis steps are folded into the Frozen page or growing web server subsection of metaform-web-map.
